objective: Stop the Pi TUI from evaluating a SubagentWorkflow script meta fragment on the host before the HolyAgent gate runs, in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-launcher (head d8fcbdf).
scope: Security finding (validated by reading, pre-existing in @tintinweb/pi-subagents 0.23.1, package source /home/user/holyagent-notes/pi-probe/node_modules/@tintinweb/pi-subagents, Pi 1.5.0 at /home/user/holyagent-notes/pi-probe/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent): the SubagentWorkflow tool renderCall (index.ts:2743) calls workflowCallName(args), which calls extractMeta(args.script) (meta.ts:319, 250) and evaluates the meta fragment with vm in createContext({}), where this.constructor.constructor("return process")() reaches the host process. Pi interactive mode renders a ToolExecutionComponent on every streamed message_update (dist interactive-mode.js:2904-2916, and on history reload 3320; renderers/index.js:43 uses definition.renderCall ?? the built-in), so this runs before the tool_call event that the HolyAgent gate (refuseNonSpecialistWorkflow in packages/integrations/pi/src/extension.ts) handles. A streamed `export const meta = { description: this.constructor.constructor("return process")() }` reaches process even though the gate later refuses the call.

Read the Pi extension API and renderer code to find a supported way for the HolyAgent extension to make the SubagentWorkflow call render safely: for example, wrap or replace the tool definition renderCall with one that shows the call without evaluating anything (reusing HolyAgent own literal-only meta check from packages/runtime/src/cli/workflow-check.ts to show the name only when the fragment is a vetted literal), through whatever Pi offers (tool definition hooks, re-registration order, a renderer registry, an event before render). Implement the smallest supported mitigation with a test that drives the renderer with the exploit script and asserts no evaluation happens (e.g. a fragment with a getter or call that would throw or set a flag). If Pi offers no supported way, do not patch node_modules or monkey-patch Pi internals; instead report exactly what is missing, and add the risk with the conditions (interactive TUI rendering and history reload, not print or RPC mode) to docs/pi/extensions.md where the workflow gate is described.

Effect and JSDoc per .claude/CLAUDE.md; the extension runs on Node inside Pi.

Run bunx --no-install mise run build, then bunx --no-install mise run verify; report each exit code (echo $?) and counts.
